department: Directorate of Public Health and Preventive Medicine, and local bodies, Government of Tamil Nadu
what_it_is: A birth must be registered where it happened. Then you get a birth certificate. Registration is done under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969.
who_can_apply: If the baby is born in a hospital, the hospital's medical officer reports the birth. If the baby is born at home, the head of the house or the nearest relative must report it.
how_to_apply: Report the birth within 21 days. In big government hospitals and PHCs, the birth certificate is given before the mother goes home. If you report it late, you need written permission and a late fee. After one year, you need an order from the Revenue Divisional Officer. Copies can be printed at e-Sevai centres. The child's name can be added free within one year.
where_to_apply: The Registrar of Births and Deaths of the place where the birth happened (Municipality, Panchayat or other local body).
fee: Free if reported within 21 days, and one free copy is given. Late fee: Rs 100 (21 to 30 days), Rs 200 (30 days to 1 year), Rs 500 (after 1 year). Extra copy (extract): Rs 200. Printing at e-Sevai: Rs 100 (Public Health) or Rs 40 (Greater Chennai Corporation).
time_limit: Report the birth within 21 days. Add the child's name within one year to avoid a late fee.
